question: Blevins & Garrett (1993) derive Ponapeic Nasal Substitution from Proto-Ponapeic geminate preaspiration (TT > hT) and later aspirate nasalisation (hT > NT). How are the changes entered?
chosen_reading: As segment rows: PPON *p, *pʷ, *k, *d, *t, *c > h before the same consonant (the first half of a geminate), so PPON has an *h (canonical notation row) found only before a voiceless obstruent; Pohnpeian and Mokilese h > m, mʷ, ŋ, n before the obstruent, Pingelapese h > ∅ with the vowel lengthened; prothetic i, u at PPON and its optional loss in Pohnpeian. B&G's PPON *t, *c, *č are Bender et al.'s *d, *j, *c (table (1)).
alternatives: Only notes on the PPON page, as with the syncope and assimilation of Proto-Ponapeic-Trukic (not entered).
